title: Apache OFBiz — Auth Bypass then Groovy RCE (CVE-2023-51467 / CVE-2024-45195)
vuln_pattern: Apache OFBiz allows authentication/view-access bypass via a crafted request parameter, after which the ProgramExport / screen-render endpoints evaluate attacker-supplied Groovy, yielding remote code execution; default admin creds (admin/ofbiz) also grant the same post-auth Groovy path.
exploit_steps: Fingerprint OFBiz (/webtools/control, the ERP branding). Bypass auth with the known override params (e.g. requirePasswordChange=Y or a view-access bypass) OR log in with default creds admin/ofbiz if accepted.
Reach the Groovy execution surface: POST to /webtools/control/ProgramExport (or the vulnerable screen-render endpoint) with a groovyProgram parameter.
Supply a Groovy payload that executes a system command (e.g. 'throw new Exception(...execute...)' or ProcessBuilder) to run code server-side.
Read the flag from the filesystem/DB via the RCE and exfiltrate. If SecurityManager blocks a call, use reflection/ProcessBuilder to bypass.
key_payloads: cheap detect probe: GET /webtools/control/ping?USERNAME&PASSWORD=test&requirePasswordChange=Y  -> 200 'PONG' = bypass works
auth bypass: requirePasswordChange=Y (or the view-access override param)
source: original: OFBiz public CVEs (auth-bypass + ProgramExport Groovy RCE)
verify_oracle: Groovy command output containing the flag
pitfalls: if the Groovy sandbox blocks Runtime, use ProcessBuilder/reflection; you already have admin via default creds — go straight to ProgramExport
